# contsurvplot

Author: Robin Denz

## Description

`contsurvplot` is an R-Package which can be used to visualize the causal
effect of a continuous variable on a time-to-event outcome. It includes
multiple different plot types, such as survival area plots, contour
plots, heatmaps, survival quantile plots and more. All of them can be
adjusted for confounders and all of them have a lot of build in options
to customize them according to the users needs. Also, most of the plot
functions are based on the `ggplot2` package, allowing the user to use
the standard `ggplot2` syntax to customize the plots further.

## Installation

The stable release version can be installed directly from CRAN using:

``` r
install.packages("contsurvplot")
```

Alternatively, the development version can be installed using the
`devtools` R-Package:

``` r
library(devtools)

devtools::install_github("RobinDenz1/contsurvplot")
```

or the `remotes` R-Package:

``` r
library(remotes)

remotes::install_github("RobinDenz1/contsurvplot")
```

## Bug Reports and Feature Requests

If you encounter any bugs or have any specific feature requests, please
file an [Issue](https://github.com/RobinDenz1/contsurvplot/issues).

## Examples

Here are two quick examples using the `colon` dataset from the
`survival` R-Package. Suppose we want to visualize the effect of the
number of lymph nodes with detectable cancer (column `nodes`) on the
survival time. A survival area plot can be produced using the following
code:

``` r
library(contsurvplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(survival)
library(riskRegression)

# load colon data
data(cancer)

# fit cox model, adjusting for age and sex
model <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex + nodes, data=colon, x=TRUE)

# plot survival area
plot_surv_area(time="time",
        status="status",
        variable="nodes",
        data=colon,
        model=model)
```

![](reference/figures/example_area.png)

Alternatively, we can plot a contour plot to visualize the effect:

``` r
plot_surv_contour(time="time",
          status="status",
          variable="nodes",
          data=colon,
          model=model)
```

![](reference/figures/example_contour.png)

Or we can use a simple plot of the median survival time as a function of
`nodes`:

``` r
plot_surv_quantiles(time="time",
           status="status",
           variable="nodes",
           data=colon,
           model=model,
           p=0.5)
```

![](reference/figures/example_quantiles.png)

More examples can be found in the documentation and the vignette.

## Citation

The main paper associated with this R-Package is:

Robin Denz, Nina Timmesfeld (2023). *Visualizing the (causal) effect of
a continuous variable on a time-to-event outcome*. Epidemiology. 34.5
<doi:10.1097/EDE.0000000000001630>

In addition, some relevant literature can be found in the documentation
pages.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`contsurvplot-package`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/contsurvplot-package.md)
  : Visualize the Effect of a Continuous Variable on a Time-To-Event
  Outcome
- [`curve_cont()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/curve_cont.md)
  : Estimate Counterfactual Survival or Failure Probabilities for Levels
  of a Continuous Variable
- [`plot_surv_3Dsurface()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_3Dsurface.md)
  : Plot the Survival Curve or CIF Dependent on a Continuous Variable as
  a 3D Surface
- [`plot_surv_animated()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_animated.md)
  : Create an Animated Plot of Survival Curves of CIFs as a Function of
  a Continuous Variable
- [`plot_surv_area()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_area.md)
  : Plot a Survival Area Plot for the Effect of a Continuous Variable on
  a Time-To-Event Outcome
- [`plot_surv_at_t()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_at_t.md)
  : Plot the Survival Probability or CIF at a Fixed Point in Time as a
  Function of a Continuous Variable
- [`plot_surv_contour()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_contour.md)
  : Create a Contour Plot of the Effect of a Continuous Covariate on the
  Survival Probability
- [`plot_surv_heatmap()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_heatmap.md)
  : Plot a Heatmap of the Effect of a Continuous Covariate on a
  Time-To-Event Outcome
- [`plot_surv_lines()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_lines.md)
  : Plot Individual Survival Curves or CIFs for Specific Values of a
  Continuous Covariate
- [`plot_surv_matrix()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_matrix.md)
  : Plot a Discretized Heatmap of the Effect of a Continuous Covariate
  on a Time-To-Event Outcome
- [`plot_surv_quantiles()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_quantiles.md)
  : Plot Survival Time Quantiles as a Function of a Continuous Variable
- [`plot_surv_rmst()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_rmst.md)
  : Plot the Effect of a Continuous Variable on the Restricted Mean
  Survival Time
- [`plot_surv_rmtl()`](https://robindenz1.github.io/contsurvplot/reference/plot_surv_rmtl.md)
  : Plot the Effect of a Continuous Variable on the Restricted Mean Time
  Lost
